candidates.title: PRT validator bridge accepts and settles a staged epoch result it did not compute and raises no alarm during the claim staging period; it detects the divergence only after acceptance, by an assert that crash-loops crisium
candidates.component: PRT player/bridge in doc/recipes (prt-bridge.lua methods:jobs acceptStagedTournamentResult job; prt-epoch.lua methods:poll EpochSealed asserts; crisium.lua main loop)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'); stands in for the honest operator
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:jobs lines ~447-454 (acceptStagedTournamentResult added for any snapshot.staged, without comparing staged.finalMachineStateHash / outputsMerkleRoot with the player's final_state_hash / outputs root); report_lost_matches (~804) runs only in methods:watch (sentinel), not in methods:tick (validator); doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua lines 89-99 (the only comparison of the settled state with the honest checkpoint, made by the NEXT epoch's listener when it applies EpochSealed(N+1), i.e. after acceptance); crisium.lua 'assert(not status.terminal ...)' / Lua error propagation -> crash loop under prt-supervise.sh
candidates.description: At the hand-off between epochs the honest operator should refuse a settled result it did not compute. The validator bridge schedules acceptStagedTournamentResult whenever an EpochStaged event of its epoch exists (snapshot.staged) and the epoch is not yet settled, whatever state was staged; it never compares the staged post-epoch state hash and outputs root with the player's own final_state_hash and outputs_merkle_root_proof. In validator mode it also reports no 'lost_match' (report_lost_matches is called only by the sentinel's watch), and no anomaly exists for 'staged result differs from the honest final state'. So when a claim other than the honest one wins the root with a different final state (for whatever reason: honest claim unjoined after its window, eliminated, or a referee defect), the honest validator itself finalizes that result as soon as the staging period ends, and the operator learns of the divergence only when the next epoch's listener applies EpochSealed(N+1) and fails 'sealed initial state differs from checkpoint' - after the claim staging period, which the Dave design (docs/epoch-lifecycle.md 'Consensus layer' and 'Settlement invariant') defines as the guardian's reaction window to foreclose a decided-but-wrong result, has already closed and the wrong state is irreversible. The assert then makes crisium exit, and prt-supervise.sh relaunches it into the same assert forever, so the operator also stops every remaining duty of older epochs (bond recoveries).
candidates.trigger: Any execution in which the root of epoch N is won by a commitment whose final state differs from the honest final state while the honest validator runs (e.g. the honest commitment is reported 'unjoined_claim' because it could not join before closure, or loses a match). The adversary or anyone stages it; after the claim staging period the honest bridge's own acceptStagedTournamentResult job settles it.
candidates.reachability: Requires the honest claim not to win the root, which under the goal's assumptions needs another defect or a violated clock assumption; the bridge behaviour itself is unconditional (any staged result is accepted). Reading only; not run.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The trigger (a divergent root winner) is not on the exclusion list, though it presupposes a failure elsewhere; the bridge's acceptance is not an exclusion. 2. Role: prt-bridge.lua/prt-epoch.lua/crisium.lua are Support ('No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI'); stands in for the honest operator. 3. High/Medium cases: none matches directly. 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. In the honest-operator role, which rule would it break? The threat model has no rule that the honest operator must refuse or alarm on a settled result it did not compute (only R13: 'The honest operator must be able to detect and refuse a mismatch between its build and a deployment'), and the goal is already broken once a wrong claim wins the root, so the acceptance adds no break of section 1. 4. Critical: no rule violated at a reachable state that I can name. 5. Low: 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model'. Preferred: Low. Alternative: Medium, if the claim staging period / guardian foreclosure is read as part of the deployment's defence that the honest operator's software must support (it is the documented reaction window of the pinned Dave design), so that finalizing a divergent result itself and detecting it only afterwards would be High (removes a margin the deployment relies on) in the honest-operator role.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Does not by itself make a wrong state settle; it removes the last off-chain defence (alarm during the staging window) and has the honest validator itself finalize a divergent epoch, then stop for good, so every later epoch starts from that state without any honest party defending or signalling.
candidates.evidence: Code reading: prt-bridge.lua jobs() adds acceptStagedTournamentResult under 'if self.cleanup and snapshot.staged and not snapshot.settled and self.claim_staging_period' only; stageTournamentResult is gated on holds(candidate) but acceptance is not; methods:tick never calls report_lost_matches; the only settled-state check is prt-epoch.lua line 90 in the next epoch's listener. Compared with Dave's documented settlement invariant (docs/epoch-lifecycle.md: acceptance asserts the staged state equals the local one; a lost root pages; the staging period is the guardian's reaction window).
candidates.test_idea: Drive a prt-bridge instance with a scripted snapshot (as the R6 journal fuzzer did) in which the root's dangling candidate is not the player's claim, EpochStaged carries a final state different from player.final_state_hash, and tip >= staged block + staging period; assert that methods:jobs returns no acceptStagedTournamentResult job and that an anomaly (e.g. 'divergent_settlement') is reported before the staging period ends. Exits 1 today because the job is scheduled and no anomaly is raised.

candidates.title: DaveConsensus never registers the genesis state as settled for outputs: the template's outputs Merkle root is not valid until epoch 0 is accepted (never, if foreclosed first), and EpochSealed(0) reports a zero outputs root
candidates.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 DaveConsensus (cartesi-rollups/contracts/src/DaveConsensus.sol) with rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.10 Application.validateOutput
candidates.role: Referee model, as the deployed referee (AUDIT.md component table)
candidates.location: DaveConsensus.sol constructor (lines 140-145: seals epoch 0 from initialMachineStateHash, emits EpochSealed(0,0,upper,initial,bytes32(0),tournament), registers nothing in _outputsMerkleRoots and leaves _lastFinalizedMachineStateHash zero); isOutputsMerkleRootValid (398-406); acceptStagedTournamentResult (272) is the only writer of _outputsMerkleRoots; Application.sol _getLastFinalizedMachineMerkleRoot falls back to the template hash for withdrawals, but validateOutput has no such fallback
candidates.description: Section 2/A1 treat the state an epoch starts from as settled; at genesis that is the valid template, whose tx buffer 'holds the outputs Merkle root of every output that the application accepted before it'. A5 says 'An outputs Merkle root is defined only for a settled canonical state ... A valid template is such a state' and 'Conversely, the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to, whenever its valid proof is presented. No party can make it stop accepting them.' DaveConsensus registers an outputs root only when an epoch's staged result is accepted. The template's root is never registered and EpochSealed(0) carries bytes32(0) as the previous outputs root. For a template that already commits to outputs, a valid proof of such an output against the template's root is rejected from deployment until epoch 0 settles (at least one root allowance plus the claim staging period), and permanently if the guardian forecloses before that, since stage and accept are notForeclosed. The withdrawal path already treats the template as the last finalized state (Application falls back to getTemplateHash), so the two paths disagree on whether the genesis state is settled. For DaveAppFactory deployments epoch 0 is empty, so after it is accepted its final state equals the template and the root becomes valid; the defect is then a delay plus the foreclosure window.
candidates.trigger: Deploy a Dave application whose valid template commits to a non-empty outputs history (e.g. an application migrated from an earlier deployment); anyone tries executeOutput with a valid proof against the template's outputs root before epoch 0 is accepted; or the guardian forecloses before epoch 0 is accepted.
candidates.reachability: Valid templates with a non-empty outputs root are explicitly allowed by section 2 ('which at genesis is the root of the empty outputs tree' only for the genesis of the application). Note the recipe player refuses such templates (R2-DFOUTPUT-1), so it cannot be exercised end to end with crisium; reachable with DaveAppFactory.newDaveApp(templateHash, ...).
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Not excluded: it does not need the deployment to violate A1-A8; the referee model implementation itself is what fails A5's converse ('unless an implementation of the referee model is what violates it'). The foreclosure path relies on the guardian, a trusted application role outside this model; if the guardian is read as outside the adversary, only the delay remains. 2. Role: DaveConsensus is 'Referee model, as the deployed referee'; 'A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it.' 3. High/Medium cases: none listed; possibly the manual/behaviour contradiction rule. 4. Critical: literally violates A5 ('the referee accepts every output that the settled state commits to, whenever its valid proof is presented') at a reachable deployment state; preferred reading Medium/Low because, without foreclosure, the outputs become acceptable (against the same root, for an empty epoch 0) once epoch 0 settles, so it is a delay of acceptance rather than a refusal, and 'what the deployment was sized for' may cover that delay. 5. Low otherwise.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (preferred: delay only); Critical under a literal reading of A5's converse with foreclosure before epoch 0 settles
candidates.threat_to_goal: Does not settle a wrong state or accept an unproved output; it is a liveness gap at the genesis hand-off: outputs the template commits to are not acceptable for the first epoch, and never if the application is foreclosed during it, although A5 says no party can stop their acceptance.
candidates.evidence: Code reading of DaveConsensus.sol (constructor, acceptStagedTournamentResult, isOutputsMerkleRootValid, getLastFinalizedMachineMerkleRoot) and Application.sol (validateOutput, _getLastFinalizedMachineMerkleRoot fallback). No chain run.
candidates.test_idea: On the local chain with the released Dave (unpatched), deploy via DaveAppFactory with a template whose tx-buffer word is the root R of a one-output tree; call Application.validateOutput(output, proof against R) right after deployment; assert it succeeds (A5 converse). Today it reverts with InvalidOutputsMerkleRoot until epoch 0 is accepted; a second assertion forecloses first and shows it reverts forever.
